title: BYOK-KMS-HSM-rotation-and-e2e-encryption-design-notes
content:
Purpose and scope

This working doc captures the proposed key management architecture and operational procedures for Redwood Inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. It focuses on three primary areas: managed KMS and HSM integration, BYOK workflows for enterprise customers, and automated key rotation with audit/evidence exports to SIEM for compliance reporting. Intended audience: security, infra, platform, product, and SRE.

High-level goals
- Ensure all customer and platform data at rest is encrypted with strong algorithms and key separation.
- Support BYOK for customers that require control over root keys and HSM-backed key material.
- Automate rotation, versioning, and proof generation for audits while minimizing service disruption.
- Provide an auditable key usage trail exported to our SIEM and evidence automation pipeline.

Design overview
1) Key hierarchy and envelope encryption- Master Customer Keys (MCKs): top-level keys used only for wrapping and unwrapping Data Encryption Keys (DEKs). MCKs are stored in customer KMS (BYOK) or Redwood-managed KMS with HSM protection.- DEKs: short-lived or long-lived keys used to encrypt volumes, object stores, and model artifacts. DEKs are stored encrypted at rest in metadata records with explicit key version pointers.- Key wrapping: all DEKs must be wrapped with the MCK using an AEAD algorithm (AES-GCM or AES-KW) to provide authenticity and confidentiality of key material.- Key versioning: each key creation or rotation creates a new version id. All ciphertext records reference a specific key id and version. Key versions are immutable once written.

2) BYOK / HSM integration patterns- Hosted customers: recommend Redwood-managed KMS (multi-tenant with strong isolation) while allowing customers to provide a BYOK MCK via external KMS integration endpoints.- Dedicated customers: prefer colocated HSMs or customer-managed Cloud KMS projects; support PKCS#11 and cloud import APIs.- Private / on-prem: support on-prem HSM appliances with attestation-based onboarding and an import token flow.- Attestation: require HSM-provided attestation statements for BYOK imports where available. If attestation is unavailable, require additional legal/operational controls.

3) Rotation strategy and SLAs- Rotation types: planned automatic rotation, manual rotation (customer-initiated), emergency rotation (compromise/revocation).- Rotation frequency: default DEK rotation: every 90 days or on config threshold; default MCK rotation policy: annual for Redwood-managed MCKs, recommended annual for customer MCKs but ultimately customer-controlled.- Rotation semantics: rotating an MCK produces a new key version; existing DEKs remain wrapped by old MCK versions until rewrapped. Rewrapping is performed lazily on DEK access or via a background rewrap job depending on service impact.- Rewrap window: aim to complete bulk rewrap within 7 days for non-critical backfills; provide real-time rewrap on first write-access for critical records.- Backward compatibility: maintain previous key versions in KMS for decryption until all ciphertexts are rewrapped and confirmed. Do not delete old key versions until a cleanup window has passed and audit evidence collected.

Operational rotation runbook (example for Redwood-managed MCK rotation)- Pre-checks: gather list of active DEKs, current key usage counts, dependent services, and outstanding migrations (JIRA SEC-4123).- Step 1: create new MCK version in KMS and mark as pending in rotation ledger.- Step 2: update routing and encrypt-new-data policy to use new MCK version for wrapping new DEKs.- Step 3: launch background rewrap worker pool with controlled concurrency to rewrap DEKs in low-traffic shards. Monitor latency and throttling metrics.- Step 4: validate read paths against rewrapped DEKs and verify integrity hashes.- Step 5: mark rotation complete and begin retention countdown for old key version.- Emergency rotation: trigger immediate create-new-key, update config to prefer new key, and flag old key for emergency retention until forensics completes.

Key lifecycle states and metadata- states: active, pending_rotation, retired, emergency_retention, deleted_pending_gc.- metadata fields to record per key: key_id, version, algorithm, created_at, rotated_at, rotation_trigger, owner, authorized_teams, allowed_usage_scopes (volume, object, model-cache), policy_tags, retention_deadline, cust_kms_ref (if BYOK).

RBAC v2 considerations for key operations- Role separation: clearly separate roles for key creation, rotation, and deletion. Minimum roles: key_admin (can create and rotate keys), key_operator (start/stop rewrap jobs), key_auditor (read-only access to key metadata and audit logs), customer_owner (BYOK owner).- Least privilege: service components use short-lived crypto credentials scoped to specific operations and key ids. SSH or long-lived API keys must never be usable for direct key unwrap/wrap operations.- Just-in-time elevation: require temporary elevation tied to a one-time approval for certain sensitive operations such as emergency key deletion. Integrate with existing SSO and approval workflows.

Audit logging schema and SIEM export mapping
- event_id: uuid
- timestamp: ISO8601
- actor: principal id (service account or user)
- actor_role: RBAC role at time of event
- operation: key_create | key_rotate | key_wrap | key_unwrap | key_deprecate | key_delete | key_policy_change | key_access_denied
- key_id: canonical key id
- key_version: version identifier
- resource_scope: e.g., volume_id, object_store_bucket, model_artifact_id
- algorithm: e.g., AES-256-GCM
- success: true|false
- latency_ms: integer
- source_ip: CIDR or IP
- correlation_id: request correlation id
- evidence_refs: list of evidence ids for automation (comma separated)

Export implementation notes
- Stream logs to internal audit topic, then enrich with user/team mapping before shipping to SIEM.
- Ensure logs include redaction markers and never contain plaintext keys or key material.
- Use a signing mechanism on exported batched evidence bundles for tamper-evidence.

Evidence automation for compliance audits
- Evidence types: rotation reports, rewrap completion manifests, attestation assertions, HSM import receipts, key policy snapshots, access review logs.
- Automation flow: nightly job exports rotation and access events into the evidence store, signs the bundle, indexes by compliance cycle id, and pushes pointer to Confluence checklist entry and SIEM.
- On-demand audit: provide pre-bundled artifacts per compliance request with integrity checksums and chain-of-custody metadata.

Operational concerns, failure modes and mitigations
- KMS outage: use multi-region secondary KMS endpoints and cached DEK unwrapping tokens with short TTL to allow read-only operations for a bounded window.
- Partial rewrap failures: job resumes with idempotent rewrap tasks; store progress checkpoints and retry with exponential backoff.
- Customer BYOK misconfiguration: provide clear validation steps, unit tests during onboarding, and a simulated wrap/unwrap test before flight.
- Key deletion: enforce multi-person approval and retention windows; soft-delete state persists for forensics.

Monitoring and alerting
- Metrics: key create rate, rotate rate, rewrap progress, failed unwrap count, KMS call error rate, average wrap latency.
- Alerts: high unwrap failure spike, rewrap falling behind SLA, unauthorized key policy change, key deletion requested without approvals.

Open questions and TODOs
- BYOK attestation standard: decide mandatory attestation formats and fallbacks for non-attestable HSMs. TODO owner: Priya.
- Retention windows for old key versions: propose 180 days default, revisit with legal. TODO owner: Mikael.
- Cost model: assess background rewrap cost impact and add to Optimize recommendations. TODO owner: Connor.

Appendix: sample CLI rotation command sequence- create new key version: redwood-kms create-key-version --key-id mck-prod-01 --algorithm AES-256-GCM --label rotation-2025-01- set prefer-new: redwood-kms set-key-flag --key-id mck-prod-01 --version rotation-2025-01 --flag prefer_new- start rewrap job: infra-rewrap start --key-id mck-prod-01 --batch-size 500 --throttle 200rps --correlation SEC-4123

Notes to reviewers
- This doc is a working draft. Expect follow-up PRs with KMS API bindings, rewrap worker implementation details, and test plans. Please add review comments inline or on the linked github PR.

End of doc
